newsitem.title: UK: LME copper rangebound, aluminium strains higher.
newsitem.headline: LME copper rangebound, aluminium strains higher.

text.p: Copper made an attempt to claw back lost territory on Thursday on the London Metal Exchange (LME) while aluminium benefitted from speculative shortcovering.
The other metals were steady to firmer, with zinc on the verge of fresh 4-1/2 year highs. But none of the other base metals came close to moving out of previously established ranges.
"Copper really is so dull after yesterday," a trader said, referring to Wednesday's dive towards $2,300 support and subsequent recovery, which had served to clear out some of the longs in the market.
Three months copper finished the midday kerb at $2,341 per tonne, compared to $2,325 on Wednesday.
But it was expected to run into resistance at the $2,346/50 area, and with volumes quite light traders expected it would fail to muster enough impetus to break higher.
The only feature was the spread widening out slightly in the kerb to around $37.
Aluminium showed more spark as it extended Wednesday's gains by pushing above the $1,650 level and the 10-day moving average of $1,662..
Traders said speculative short-covering was helping aluminium ratchet higher after a dip on Tuesday below $1,650 had uncovered good consumer buying from all quarters on Wednesday.
It finished the kerb $17 stronger at $1,664.
Traders said the latest output figures from the International Primary Aluminium Institute (IPAI) were supportive.
In February daily average primary aluminium output fell to 57,000 tonnes compared with 57,600 in January and 50,500 in February 1996, the IPAI said.
A close above $1,650 on Thursday would be bullish, traders said.
Zinc built on Wednesday's positive close and looked like trying for fresh 4-1/2 year highs, finishing the kerb at $1,306, a gain of $9.
"From a chart perspective, if zinc is able to close just above these levels, more gains will follow," a trader said.
Tin was barely easier at $6,020, down $15, and trading volumes were very thin, traders said.
But tin cash/threes continued displaying volatility in the nearby dates, with cash threes moving into a $15 contango, compared to late Wednesday's $10/$13 backwardation.
Cash/April eased to level, from around $20 backwardation on Wednesday. The market was thin and spreads were flaring and contracting without being traded on the floor.
Lead was firmer with the rest of the complex at $5 up $696, while alloy was last indicated at $1,553/55, compared to $1,540.
